source.title: The Social Origins of Human Prosociality

confidence_rationale: A well-regarded synthesis arguing that other-benefiting helping starts as participatory activity WITHOUT prosocial intent in the first year and becomes autonomous and prosocially-MOTIVATED over the second year. This corroborates the 'appetitive other-bound stream matures comparatively late and gradually' half of Q-073. Confidence moderate because it is a conceptual review (not a single dataset), and because it emphasises social SCAFFOLDING (caregiver-driven) rather than an intrinsic ordering of affective streams.
failure_signatures: Early helping is participatory and lacks genuine prosocial intent; if REE treats an early other-bound APPETITIVE signal as already intentional/benefit-directed, that over-attributes structure the developmental data say is not yet present.

The review attributes the maturation of prosociality largely to BIDIRECTIONAL caregiver scaffolding, not to an autonomous internal ordering of affective streams -- so 'the appetitive stream matures later' may be environmentally driven rather than an intrinsic architectural ordering REE could assume substrate-internally.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Helping behaviour begins in participatory activities without prosocial intent in the first year of life and becomes increasingly autonomous and motivated by genuine prosocial intent over the second year; this development emerges through bidirectional social interactions in which caregivers scaffold and infants play active roles.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports the 'late and gradual' maturation of REE's other-bound APPETITIVE / liking-wanting stream (the drive to confer benefit on another). Combined with the Davidov entry (distress-concern online by ~3 months) and the Tallot/Sullivan entry (threat system substrate-gated), this triangulates Q-073's ordering: the suffering/concern channel is available earlier and the genuinely benefit-directed appetitive channel consolidates later -- the protection-first shape REE encodes in MECH-408.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper's central thesis is that prosociality is SOCIALLY SCAFFOLDED -- driven by caregiver interaction -- not that there is an intrinsic, substrate-internal ordering of affective streams. So it supports the OBSERVED ordering but offers an alternative (environmental) MECHANISM for it, which weakens any inference that REE should hard-code the ordering as architecture rather than let it emerge from a training curriculum. It also does not test the exploitation-vulnerability hypothesis directly.
mapping.source_context: Conceptual review / Current Directions synthesis of the developmental-psychology literature on the emergence of helping in the first two years of human life.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality good but it is a synthesis/position review rather than primary data, so I cap source_quality below the empirical-paper band. Mapping fidelity moderate -- 'prosocial helping' is a fair proxy for the other-bound appetitive stream. Transfer risk moderate; the scaffolding-vs-architecture distinction is the main reason this only corroborates rather than confirms an intrinsic REE ordering.
